title: Squillions: How Money Laundering Won
ai_summary:
• A recent report reveals a surge in money laundering using cryptocurrency, totaling $8.6 billion in 2022.
• Sophisticated techniques, including peer-to-peer transactions and dark web markets, are employed by launderers.
• Regulatory bodies face challenges in tracing and preventing these illicit transactions efficiently.
student_angle: The rise of cryptocurrency's use in money laundering highlights a pressing security concern, but it may not directly impact entry-level job opportunities. However, studying data science and machine learning can help develop the skills necessary to combat these emerging threats in the tech industry.
